title: Dovetail drawer
summary: the opening in, the joinery out
description: A dovetailed drawer sized from the hole it must fill: give the opening and running clearance, the board thickness, the joint and the timber, and the Jig lays out the tails by the old rules and refuses a gap a wet season would close.
process: Hand-cut or machine-cut dovetails or box joints, plough groove, glue-up

difficulty.rationale: Multi-body booleans, sketch patterns whose count changes the topology, table-driven layout and closed-form volumes.

standards: W. Fairham, Woodwork Joints (1921, Project Gutenberg 21531): dovetail inclination 1 in 8, never steeper than 1 in 6; pins on front and back, tails on the sides; 1/4 in. lap on a drawer front; through dovetails at the back
G. D. Huey, My Take on Dovetail Angles, Popular Woodworking, 2008: 1:6 (9 deg) for softwoods, 1:8 (7 deg) for hardwoods
C. Becksvoort, Don't Fear the Hand-Cut Dovetail, Fine Woodworking 238: 50 % tails strongest but machine-looking, 70 to 80 % tails by hand

A. C. Van Draanen, An A-Z of Making and Fitting Drawers, Fine Woodworking 11 (1978): sides 8 to 12 mm, front at least 20 mm, groove at most half the side, plywood bottom 3 to 6 mm, back lower than the sides by about 6 mm
T. McLaughlin, Make and Fit a Dovetailed Drawer, Fine Woodworking 294: gap about 1/32 in, half-blind front, through back above the groove
G. Hack, How to Build Solid Drawer Bottoms, Fine Woodworking 213: back stops at the top of the grooves, bottom slides in after assembly
K. Burton, Tablesaw Dovetails, Woodcraft: full-width half pins keep a groove inside the pin
USDA FPL Wood Handbook table 13-5 (2010), as reprinted in FPL-RP-711 and a Wood Movement chart: dimensional change coefficients
The Wood Database: average dried densities
materials: Walnut or chosen hardwood, 20 to 32 mm (front)
Maple or chosen timber, 8 to 14 mm (sides and back)
Turned maple knob with wedged tenon, or brass knob on an M4 screw
PVA glue, one screw per 200 mm through the bottom into the back
